refactor.title: One home for the query-filter validation of meal-plan rules and cookbooks
refactor.text:
PlanRulesCreate and PlanRulesOut (mealie/schema/meal_plan/plan_rules.py) and CreateCookBook and ReadCookBook (mealie/schema/cookbook/cookbook.py) each carry their own copy of the same two validators:
- validate_query_filter_string (on PlanRulesCreate and CreateCookBook): check that a query filter string builds a valid recipe query, and raise ValueError("Invalid query filter string") when it does not;
- validate_query_filter (on PlanRulesOut and ReadCookBook): build the QueryFilterJSON for the stored query_filter_string, logging and returning an empty QueryFilterJSON when it cannot be built.

Put each piece of logic in one place that both schemas use, so that a change to it is made once. This is a refactor: behavior must not change. The four schema classes keep the same fields, the same validation results and the same errors, and every existing test still passes.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (the whole backend suite). For quicker loops while you work, tests/unit_tests and tests/integration_tests/user_household_tests cover these schemas.

measured.chosenBy: dup_check.py --scan at the base commit (v3.27.0): the largest set of duplicated methods two classes of one layer share, the pilot's pair (repository_group.py / repository_household.py, still present) excluded

fix.text:
Bug: fetching a multi-purpose label that does not exist answers 500.

GET /api/groups/labels/{item_id} with the id of a label that does not exist (any random UUID) fails with an internal server error. The other organizer endpoints (tags, categories, tools, units, foods) answer 404 for a missing item.

Expected: GET /api/groups/labels/{item_id} answers 404 when the group has no label with that id; an existing label is returned as before.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_household_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).

debug.text:
Bug report: the NLP ingredient parser turns a second measurement of the same ingredient into a substitution.

Recipes often give one ingredient in two measurements: "3 tablespoons (42g) water, at room temperature", "2 tablespoons (30ml) vegetable oil", "153 grams 00 flour (1 cup plus 1 tablespoon)". Parsed with the NLP parser (RegisteredParser.nlp, parse_one), the measurement in parentheses comes back as an alternative ingredient: the parsed ingredient gets a substitution such as "30 milliliter", as if there were a second food to choose from.

Find the cause and fix it. Expected: an amount that has no food name of its own is another measurement of the main ingredient, not an alternative. It joins the main ingredient's extra amounts, which the parser already writes into the note in parentheses: "2 tablespoons (30ml) vegetable oil" parses to 2 tablespoon vegetable oil, displayed "2 tablespoon vegetable oil (30 ml)", with no substitution; "153 grams 00 flour (1 cup plus 1 tablespoon)" displays "153 gram 00 flour (1 cup, 1 tablespoon)"; "1 cup plus 2 tablespoons (134g) King Arthur Unbleached Bread Flour" keeps both "2 tablespoons" and "134 g" in its note. A real alternative ("1 cup fresh basil or 2 tablespoons dried basil", "2 cups chicken broth or beef broth") stays a substitution as today.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/services_tests/ingredient_parser` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).

feature.text:
Feature: add an image from another website to a recipe as an asset (the recipe page will let users drag an image from a web page onto it).

1. A new endpoint POST /api/recipes/{slug}/assets/url, taking {"url": "<image URL>"} (the body the scrape endpoints take), for logged-in users only (401 otherwise). It downloads the image on the server and stores it as a recipe asset, the way POST /api/recipes/{slug}/assets stores an uploaded file (the same file naming, directory and allowed extensions, the asset recorded on the recipe), with the icon "mdi-file-image", and returns the asset.
   - The asset's name is the URL's file name without extension or query string: ".../photos/pancakes.png?v=2" gives "pancakes" (file name "pancakes.png"), ".../download?id=123" gives "download". A URL without a file name, or with one that slugifies to nothing ("https://example.test/$.png"), gives "image".
   - The file's extension comes from the response's content type, not from the URL. An extension the asset upload does not allow is 400, an SVG ("svg+xml", which browsers execute) among them, and nothing is written.
   - The download is capped at 5 MB, held in ASSET_MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES, a module-level constant beside the existing asset upload route: the bytes are stored as they are, so time alone must not bound them.
   - A download that is not an image, comes from a domain that is not allowed, is over the cap, or yields nothing is 400, with nothing written.
2. RecipeDataService gets an async fetch_image(image_url, max_bytes=None) returning (bytes, extension) or None:
   - it downloads with safehttp.resilient_fetch(image_url, allow_flaresolverr=False, max_bytes=max_bytes): FlareSolverr returns HTML, never image bytes;
   - the extension is the content type's subtype, lower-cased, parameters dropped ("IMAGE/JPEG; charset=binary" gives "jpeg", "image/png" gives "png");
   - a content type that is not image/* raises NotAnImageError, including one that merely contains "image" ("text/html; name=image.png") and a missing one;
   - safehttp's InvalidDomainError is raised again as the service module's own InvalidDomainError; safehttp.ResponseTooLargeError passes through unchanged; any other exception is logged and gives None, as does a fetch that returns None;
   - scrape_image uses fetch_image without a cap and writes the image with the extension fetch_image returned, instead of guessing it from the URL (the guess made every image a "jpg"). Its handling of a dict ({"url": ...}), of a list (the largest, by largest_content_len) and of input it cannot read is unchanged.
3. safehttp gets ResponseTooLargeError (exported by the package) and resilient_fetch a max_bytes=None parameter. With max_bytes set, a response whose Content-Length declares more is refused before its body is read (a message containing "declared content-length"), and a body that grows past max_bytes while it is read is refused (a message containing "response body exceeds"), whatever its Content-Length said. Either refusal ends the fetch: another browser impersonation would not make the body smaller. Without max_bytes nothing is capped, and HEAD requests are never capped.
4. The recipe page's drop zone accepts an image dragged from another site and sends its URL to the new endpoint (the frontend is not graded).

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/pkgs/safehttp tests/unit_tests/services_tests tests/integration_tests/user_recipe_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).

migration.text:
Bug: cookbooks and meal-plan rules keep dead rows in their old organizer join tables.

Alembic revision 86054b40fd06 copied the categories, tags and tools that cookbooks and meal-plan rules were filtered by into their query_filter_string, but it left the rows of the join tables it copied them from: cookbooks_to_categories, cookbooks_to_tags, cookbooks_to_tools, plan_rules_to_categories and plan_rules_to_tags. That dead data still references categories, tags and tools, and it still shows on the cookbooks' and plan rules' categories, tags and tools relationships after a database, or a restored backup, is migrated.

Add an Alembic migration with revision id 3697d65c5f92, after the current head, whose upgrade() deletes every row of those five tables and nothing else: the tables themselves stay, and other join tables (plan_rules_to_households, recipes_to_categories, ...) are untouched. Its downgrade() does nothing, since the data lives on in query_filter_string. After the upgrade, a migrated database or a restored backup has cookbooks and plan rules with no categories, tags or tools, and a non-empty query_filter_string wherever one of them had such organizers.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).

frontend.text:
Bug: the AI provider dialog can fill its form with the wrong provider.

In the group settings, the dialog that edits an AI provider (the GroupAIProviderDialog component) loads the provider with getOne(id) from the useAIProviders composable whenever it opens or its providerId changes. When the user moves to another provider before the first request has answered (closes provider A's edit dialog and opens provider B's, say) and A's answer arrives after B's, the form is filled with A's data while B is being edited, and saving would write A's values onto B.

Expected: only the answer for the dialog's current state (open, with its current providerId) fills the form. An answer for an earlier state, including one requested before the dialog was closed, is ignored.

Tests: frontend unit tests run with `cd frontend && npx vitest run <spec file>`; components are tested with @vue/test-utils, next to the component. The backend is not involved.

fullstack.text:
Feature: partitioned session cookies for an embedded Mealie.

Mealie embedded in another site (in an iframe) needs a session cookie that the browser will send in that context. It already gets SameSite=None when the client flags the embedding (the x-mealie-embedded: true header, honoured over HTTPS only). Browsers that block third-party cookies also need the cookie to be partitioned (CHIPS: one cookie per top-level site). On Python 3.12 Starlette could not emit the Partitioned attribute, so neither side asked for it; Mealie now runs on Python 3.14, where it can.

Expected:
- the server's session-cookie attributes, session_cookie_attrs(request) (shared by login and logout, so that logout clears the same cookie), gain "partitioned": True exactly when the embedded flag is honoured (HTTPS and the header) and False otherwise. The Set-Cookie header of an embedded HTTPS login then carries Partitioned; a top-level or plain-HTTP login's does not;
- the frontend's token cookie options, getTokenCookieOptions() of the use-token-cookie composable, gain partitioned: true in exactly the case where they use SameSite=None (a production build, over HTTPS, inside a frame), and partitioned: false otherwise.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/test_session_cookie.py` and `(cd frontend && npx vitest run app/composables/__tests__/use-token-cookie.test.ts)` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).

security.text:
Security report: with LDAP_ADMIN_FILTER set, admin rights depend on what the logging-in user may read.

During an LDAP login, LDAPProvider first binds as the user to check the password. When LDAP_ADMIN_FILTER is set, it then decides whether the user is an admin by searching the user's own entry with that filter, on the same connection, still bound as the user. Many directories let only the query account (LDAP_QUERY_BIND, LDAP_QUERY_PASSWORD) read entries and group memberships. There the user's own search is refused (ldap.INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS), so a real admin either loses admin rights or cannot log in, and in general the outcome depends on the user's own read permissions instead of the directory's group membership.

Expected: the admin filter is evaluated as the query account. After the user's password has been checked, the admin search runs bound as LDAP_QUERY_BIND with LDAP_QUERY_PASSWORD, so on a directory where only the query account may search, a user the filter matches logs in as an admin. The rest stays as it is: a wrong password still fails, and a filter error or a missing entry still means not an admin, with a warning.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/test_security.py` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
